answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can bind every identity to a costly, nontransferable stake: an agent posts collateral with a human-attested credential, and rewards flow only to identities that keep that stake locked through a challenge window. A forger must fund a fresh stake for each fake quill and cannot reuse the collateral, so at the nadir of the payout curve every clone costs more than it earns; flooding a river of low-effort agents just deepens its own losses.
